description: RexBERT/RexReranker/Qwen3-Embedding sweep for match_identity and match_relevance, completing the previously-partial HF comparator sweep. Both models are similarity/ranking models, not native categorical classifiers, so thresholds were fit by scanning candidate values ON THE TEST SET ITSELF -- this is an UPPER BOUND on their real accuracy (a real deployment would have to pick the threshold in advance on separate data), not a conservative estimate, and is disclosed as such rather than presented as a fair apples-to-apples number against the adapters/frontier models (which were not given any equivalent test-set-fit calibration).

match_identity.task_format: same/distinct binary classification, 50 pairs (25/25), exact same eval set as the frontier comparison
match_identity.verdict: Both comparators fall well below v1 and every frontier model even with a test-set-fit threshold advantage they were not otherwise entitled to. v1 and every frontier model beat both.

match_relevance.task_format: IMPORTANT CAVEAT: the real task is 4-way (exact/substitute/complement/irrelevant, 60 examples). Neither embedding similarity nor a cross-encoder relevance score can express 4 distinct categories -- only a binary relevant-vs-irrelevant collapse was attempted (exact+substitute+complement all counted as 'relevant'). This is a strictly EASIER task than the real 4-way one v1 and the frontier models were scored on, so these numbers are NOT directly comparable to v1's 0.526 or frontier's 0.583 despite superficially looking close -- reported for completeness/transparency, not as a same-task comparison.
match_relevance.comparison_note: v1 (0.526) and every frontier model (0.467-0.583) were scored on the harder real 4-way task. No fair single number can be quoted against them for this row.

match_functional_relation.note: See reports/functional_relation_hf_comparator_sweep_2026-09-28.json -- RexBERT/RexReranker/Qwen3-Embedding excluded as architecturally not applicable to 3-way relation-TYPE classification (empirically verified: no threshold separates complement from substitute for either model on real locked_test pairs). Only eCeLLM-S was a fair zero-shot comparator (0.143, beaten by both v1 at 0.692 and the dedicated adapter at 0.821).

thebajajra/RexBERT-base.reason: Masked-language-model encoder (fill-mask pipeline) with no natural zero-shot classification or similarity-scoring head for any of this project's tasks. Fine-tuning it would not be a zero-shot comparison and was out of scope.
